newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to take first U.S. fighters in April - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to take first U.S. fighters in April - paper.

text.p: Taiwan will take delivery on April 26 of the first two of 150 F-16 fighter planes bought from the United States to strengthen its air defences against rival China, local media said on Thursday.

The Independence Morning Post quoted unidentified military sources as saying U.S. pilots would deliver the two warplanes to a U.S. base in Okinawa, Japan, for pick-up by Taiwanese pilots, who would fly them to Taiwan.
The Defence Ministry declined to comment, but has said it would take delivery of the first batch of the F-16s, purchased in a 1992 deal that angered China, some time after April.
Taiwan also expects in May to take delivery of the first of 60 Mirage fighters purchased from France before Paris, acceding to Chinese pressure, agreed to stop arming the island.

Both the F-16s and the Mirages are expected to play vital roles in Nationalist-ruled Taiwan's air defences against China, which, since the sides split after a civil war in 1949, has vowed to retake the island -- by force if necessary.
China, which regards any advanced military sale to Taiwan by foreign powers as an encroachment on its own sovereignty, had protested vehemently against the F-16 and Mirage deals.

China held war games and missile tests near Taiwan before the island's first direct presidential election in March 1996 in what Beijing acknowledged was a warning to Taiwanese voters not to drop a pledge to reunify with the mainland.
